senses.gloss:
haviryajña
(‘a sacrifice in which हविस् [uncooked oblatory material] is used’)
------------------------------------------
Vedic sacrifices called yajñas or yāgas are an ancient religious institution. They have exercised a tremendous influence on the Hindu society over the millennia.
They are generally classified into three groups: pākayajñas, haviryajñas and somayāgas.
Though the word ‘havis’ means any oblatory material, it generally refers to uncooked materials like barley, rice, milk or ghee.
Seven haviryajñas are mentioned in the śrautasūtra literature. They are: अग्न्याधेय, अग्निहोत्र, दर्शपूर्णमास, चातुर्मास्य, आग्रयण, Nirūḍhapaśu-बन्ध and सौत्रामणी.
All these are performed in the three Vedic fires viz., गार्हपत्य, दक्षिणा and आहवनीय.

havirdhāna
(‘oblation receptacle’)
------------------------------------------
Among the वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, the सोम-yāgas form an important group. The juice of the सोम creeper is the main oblation material in these yāgas. The creepers are brought to the place of sacrifice in two carts. Each of these carts is called ‘havirdhāna’.
A shed called ‘havirdhānamaṇṭapa’ is constructed within the महावेदि (a trapezium shaped altar for the सोम sacrifice), to the east of the sadas (place of assembly of the priests) according to specified dimensions. The two carts are placed here after cleaning and washing them, on the day before the actual pressing.

havis
(‘through this, it is given’, ‘oblatory material’)
------------------------------------------
Vedic sacrifices needed several materials that could be offered into the duly consecrated fire as oblations. Such materials were called ‘havis’.
Five kinds of materials were recommended as हविस्: औषध (products of trees and plants), payas (milk), पशु (animals), सोम (juice of the सोम creeper) and आज्य (clarified butter).
Rice, barley, their products like चरु (porridge) or पुरोडाश (rice-cake) were included under ‘auṣadha’.

haviṣya
(‘that which is fit to be offered in sacrifice’)
------------------------------------------
Haviṣya or haviṣyānna is any ड़ोओद् fit or pure enough to be offered in a sacrifice.
Food normally consumed by the forest hermits (like milk, सोम juice, boiled ड़ोओद् without spices), ड़ोओद् to be offered to the ब्राह्मणस् that are invited for śrāddhas and also to be taken by the inviter, is also haviṣyānna.
Those observing religious vows either as प्रायश्चित्त (expiation for sins) or even otherwise, are also expected to subsist on haviṣyānna during that period.
The haviṣyānna generally prepared out of boiled grains like rice, wheat and barley, but without spices or salt, being pure and sāttvika, was believed to aid the concerned persons with a better frame of मिन्द् for the observance of the ritual.
